intro.title: Type useRef for DOM and custom objects
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that uses the useRef hook to interact with a DOM element and manage a custom object. You'll learn how to properly type useRef for both DOM references (like an input field) and mutable values (like a counter object). The core concept is using TypeScript's generics with useRef to ensure type safety and avoid runtime errors. You'll work with React, TypeScript, and the useRef hook to create a practical example. By the end, you'll understand how to declare and use typed refs for different purposes in your components.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications, typing `useRef` is essential when building interactive UI components that need to directly manipulate DOM elements or manage persistent object references. For example, in a dashboard with live charts, you might use a typed `useRef` to access a canvas element for drawing real-time data visualizations, ensuring TypeScript knows it's an `HTMLCanvasElement`. Similarly, in a complex form with dynamic validation, you could type a `useRef` to store a custom validation rules object, preventing runtime errors by enforcing its structure. This pattern also appears in modals or dropdown menus where you need to programmatically focus an input field or measure an element's dimensions, providing type safety and better developer experience.
